requirements.evidence: The model, policies, pick route and the three pages are implemented and mostly match the contract (app/Models/Entity.php:17-37, app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-38, routes/web.php:27-50, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:63-97), but the required docs/database-schema.md update is absent, visible UI text is hardcoded (resources/views/livewire/entity/settings.blade.php:14,20,24; members.blade.php:11,36) and assignRole can demote the owner (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:74).

conventions.evidence: Policies, deliberate $fillable and named indexes follow project style (app/Models/Entity.php:15, database/migrations/2026_10_29_034824_create_entity_memberships_table.php:21,25), but domain writes live in components instead of app/Actions/* (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:34-97; Members.php:30-101), public inputs lack #[Validate] attributes (Members.php:22; Settings.php:20-24), authorization in the pick route bypasses policies (routes/web.php:28) and docs/CHANGELOG are not updated.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes server-side and resolves client-controlled ids before acting (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:57-63,80-86; Settings.php:67-91) and the bound entity is #[Locked] (Settings.php:17-18), but assignRole does not protect the owner's membership (Members.php:74) and `verified` is not registered as persistent Livewire middleware (routes/web.php:40-46).

tests.evidence: No tests/ files appear anywhere in change.diff; the only test-related addition is a CI workflow (.github/workflows/tests.yml:1-11) that contains no tests.

simplicity.evidence: Components are small and direct with no speculative abstractions (app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:1-27), but there is minor duplication: repeated membership lookups in app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:21-38 and a redundant owner guard after the policy already rejects it (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:86-90).

readability.evidence: Short, well-named methods and consistent Blade/Bulma markup (resources/views/livewire/entity/dashboard.blade.php:1-14), but queries and a hardcoded 'admin' live in the template (settings.blade.php:34) and the membership loop lacks wire:key (members.blade.php:21).

scope.evidence: Most files serve the task, but two unrelated workflow files are added: .github/workflows/tests.yml:1-11 and an empty .github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, although the project requires a test for every feature and happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action.
assignRole updates any membership in the entity without excluding the owner, so an admin can demote the owner and leave the entity with no owner, permanently losing settings and ownership transfer.

Visible strings ('Add', 'Remove', 'Save', 'Delete entity', 'Slug', role labels) are hardcoded instead of coming from lang/*/ui.php, and no lang keys were added for them, so the pt_BR UI shows English.
The task explicitly requires reading and updating docs/database-schema.md, but the new entities/entity_memberships tables and their indexes are not documented.

Domain writes (entity update/delete, ownership transfer, membership add/assign/remove) are performed directly in Livewire components instead of dedicated app/Actions/* classes as the conventions require.
The duplicate-member error uses a hardcoded English sentence instead of a translation key, unlike the rest of the UI.
Public input properties have no #[Validate] attributes; validation is only inline via $this->validate(), deviating from the project's documented #[Validate] + $this->validate() pattern.
entity.pick authorizes with an inline abort_unless(membershipFor(...)) inside a route closure instead of going through a policy/gate as the conventions require.
delete() removes memberships before deleting the entity outside a transaction, so a failure in between permanently loses membership rows.
Unrelated CI files were added: tests.yml runs php artisan test without installing PHP dependencies or a database (it will fail) and deploy-dev.yml is an empty file; neither is part of the task.
The `verified` middleware (unlike `auth`) is not registered as persistent Livewire middleware, so it is not re-applied on /livewire/update requests; policies still guard every action.
targetMembershipId is a client-writable property with no validation or #[Locked]; impact is limited because it is re-resolved against the entity and role-checked before use.
The template runs a query and hardcodes 'admin' instead of receiving the list from the component or using UserRole::Admin->value.
The @foreach over memberships has no wire:key, which can make Livewire reuse the wrong row after a removal.
Role select and Remove button are rendered for every viewer, including employees who will receive 403, leaving dead controls instead of gating them on the policy.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership data model, policies, pick route and the dashboard, members and settings Livewire pages, and largely matches the contract. It nevertheless ships no tests at all, leaves docs/database-schema.md and the UI translations incomplete, and lets an admin demote the owner by assigning a new role; the unrelated CI workflow files add scope noise and one of them cannot pass. This needs substantial rework before merging.
